examples.question_text: Solve $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{8}=\dfrac{\sin45^{\circ}}{16}$ for the acute angle $\theta$, correct to the nearest minute.

examples.solution_text:
$\theta$ is opposite $AC=8$ km. The complete opposite pair is $\angle A=60^{\circ}$ and $BC=12$ km.

$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{\sin\theta}{8}&=\dfrac{\sin60^{\circ}}{12}\\\sin\theta&=\dfrac{8\sin60^{\circ}}{12}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8\sin60^{\circ}}{12}\right)\\&=35.2643\ldots^{\circ}\\&\approx35.3^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\theta$ is opposite $AB=12$ m. The complete opposite pair is $\angle A=30^{\circ}$ and $BC=8$ m.

$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{\sin\theta}{12}&=\dfrac{\sin30^{\circ}}{8}\\\sin\theta&=\dfrac{12\sin30^{\circ}}{8}\end{aligned}$

Let $\alpha$ be the acute angle returned by inverse sine.

$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12\sin30^{\circ}}{8}\right)\\&=48.5903\ldots^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Since $\theta$ is obtuse, use the supplement.

$\begin{aligned}\theta&=180^{\circ}-48.5903\ldots^{\circ}\\&=131.4096\ldots^{\circ}\\&\approx131.4^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The chosen angle is compatible with the triangle: $131.4096\ldots^{\circ}+30^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$.
